title: Apply OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and Session Token Lifecycle
prompt: Threat-model and test a browser-based PKCE sign-in with verified redirect, state, token rotation, concurrent refresh, revocation, logout, and server authorisation.
successCriteria: The asset, attacker, boundary, abuse path, assumptions, and residual risk are explicit.
The implementation enforces least privilege at the authoritative boundary and preserves safe failure.
Adversarial tests plus rotation, revocation, migration, monitoring, recovery, and ownership are documented.
hints: Attempt the attack before and after the control so evidence demonstrates the intended property.
Inspect the release artifact and server contract, not only source or UI behaviour.
solutionOutline: Create the threat and data-flow model, then select the narrowest sufficient control.
Implement and attack the control, document limitations, and rehearse lifecycle and incident paths.
verification: Run bypass, replay/substitution, account-switch, failure, and recovery scenarios.
Review evidence and residual risk with the owner who can accept or remediate it.
